more.title: Fossil long known as world's oldest reptile dethroned
more.summary: For nearly 30 years, a small fossil from Scotland has been celebrated as one of the earliest known reptiles. A new study out today in Nature and led by researchers at the American Museum of Natural History and the University of Oxford, in collaboration with the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility, is rewriting that story.

more.title: Even high-altitude forests in Switzerland are now weakened by frequent droughts, making natural hazards more dangerous
more.summary: Due to global warming, Swiss forests are now at a tipping point where summer droughts are overwhelming trees' tolerance and resilience, scientists have shown. That bodes ill for people in the valleys because forests form their first line of defense against avalanches, rockfalls, landslides and floods.

more.title: Why some Ukrainian refugees struggle to rebuild their careers after arriving in Canada
more.summary: The Russian invasion of Ukraine continues into 2026, with millions of Ukrainians displaced around the world. Many arrived in host countries with professional experience, degrees and specialized skills. Yet displacement often leaves highly educated refugees unable to continue their previous careers.

more.title: Community-led archaeology project uncovers a major monastery of medieval Scotland
more.summary: Community-led archaeology has uncovered the remains of an early medieval monastery in Argyll, western Scotland, identifying it as the high-ranking ecclesiastical center of Lios Mòr, previously known only from historical references and local traditions.

more.title: Key protein for cells' gene regulation needs a chaperone to do its job
more.summary: A protein that's essential to every cell's ability to turn off unnecessary genes is well known for its key function of compacting genes and its connection to cancer when it undergoes mutation. But until now, scientists weren't quite sure how the protein gets where it needs to go to keep genes bound up so they aren't activated.

more.title: Confronting demons: How acoustic and AI technology brought ancient Etruscan tombs back to life
more.summary: Although it is not always obvious, sound guides how we experience the world around us. And the latest archaeoacoustic techniques show that even the world's earliest architects understood this.
